meta.statement: This is a self-assessment. No third-party audit or certification has been performed. The register, the method and the accepted risks are published so that the assessment can be independently checked by anyone with a clone of the repository.

out_of_scope: web/ — the Vue single-page frontend, assessed separately
packages/ — the C# and TypeScript client SDKs, assessed separately
Operator deployment configuration beyond the shipped Helm chart
cmd/bridge and the honeypot profile, which are non-default deployment modes
scope.asvs_level_note: Every ASVS 5.0.0 requirement at L1 and L2 is classified. L3 requirements are outside the declared level; where one is nevertheless satisfied or deliberately not satisfied it is recorded anyway rather than omitted.

meta.claim: Every requirement in scope is classified Met, Accepted Risk, or Not Applicable. There are no unclassified requirements and no open Gap findings. Every Met requirement names at least one test in tests/compliance/ that runs on every CI build. Every Accepted Risk carries a rationale, a compensating control, a residual-risk statement, a revisit condition and a named accepting party. Every Not Applicable requirement carries the reason it does not apply.
meta.no_percentages: This register deliberately publishes no coverage percentage. A percentage requires a weighting model and a denominator; publishing the register instead lets a reader compute whatever figure they consider meaningful, and check it.

identifier_namespaces.AR-nn: docs/security.md. The engineering accepted-risk log, AR-1 through AR-18.
identifier_namespaces.CR-nn: this register, the accepted_risks map below. Compliance-scoped.
identifier_namespaces.why: Both documents once numbered their risks AR-nn from the same sequence, and four numbers meant different things in the two files: AR-14, AR-15, AR-17 and AR-18. A reader who followed a cross-reference landed on an unrelated risk, and docs/COMPLIANCE.md asserted the closure of AR-16 while docs/security.md AR-16 was open. The register's identifiers were renumbered to CR-nn so the namespaces cannot collide again. Go source and tests/attack cite AR-nn and always mean docs/security.md.

CR-14.title: The absolute session lifetime defaults well above the AAL2 recommendation
CR-14.security_md: Register-scoped. docs/security.md owns the AR-nn namespace and defines a different risk under this number; the two lists are deliberately disjoint.
CR-14.rationale: NIST SP 800-63B-4 section 2.2.3 sets two advisory figures at AAL2: an overall reauthentication timeout of no more than 24 hours and an inactivity timeout of no more than 1 hour. The inactivity half closed: VAULT_INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT defaults to 1 hour and AuthService.enforceSessionInactivity terminates a refresh-token family that goes unused for longer, measured from the family's last rotation, failing closed when that instant cannot be read. ASVS V7.3.1, NIST 800-63B-4 section 5.2 and NIST 800-53 AC-12 moved to Met on it, and V7.1.1 moved with them because both timeouts are now documented and the deviation below is justified in docs/config.md. What remains is one figure: the overall timeout defaults to 720 hours, because a 24-hour default would force a daily re-login on a general-purpose authentication server whose deployments are not all AAL2.
CR-14.compensating_control: The inactivity timeout is the control that most limits the exposure: a session held for 720 hours has to be rotated at least once an hour for 30 days. Access tokens live 15 minutes; every refresh re-checks account state, re-verifies the device fingerprint, and rotates the token single-use with family revocation on replay; the absolute family bound is enforced and fails closed; users and administrators can revoke all sessions; the per-user session cap bounds how many can exist. An operator who needs the AAL2 figure can set VAULT_MAX_SESSION_LIFETIME=24h today.
CR-14.residual_risk: The shipped default permits a client that refreshes at least once an hour to hold one session for 30 days without reauthenticating.
CR-14.revisit_when: Any deployment claims AAL2 conformance to a third party rather than self-assessing, in which case the default must move to 24 hours. Also revisit if a customer contract specifies a maximum session age.
CR-14.cost_of_closing: One constant, plus a documented migration note: shortening the default logs every existing session out on upgrade.

CR-20.title: Authenticator loss is handled by operator escrow, not by repeated identity proofing
CR-20.security_md: Register-scoped. docs/security.md owns the AR-nn namespace and defines a different risk under this number; the two lists are deliberately disjoint.
CR-20.rationale: ASVS 5.0.0 V6.4.4 requires evidence of identity proofing at the same level as enrollment when a factor is lost. vault42 performs no identity proofing at enrollment, so there is no level to match; the requirement presumes an identity-proofing CSP that vault42 is not.
CR-20.compensating_control: Backup codes are issued at enrollment; beyond those, recovery requires the operator-held escrow, which needs a private key held offline and outside the system.
CR-20.residual_risk: Account recovery ultimately rests on operator process rather than on a technical proof of identity.
CR-20.revisit_when: vault42 gains an identity-proofing step at enrollment.
CR-20.cost_of_closing: Not applicable without an identity-proofing capability.

CR-22.title: Identity provider session lifetime is not tracked
CR-22.security_md: Register-scoped. docs/security.md owns the AR-nn namespace and defines a different risk under this number; the two lists are deliberately disjoint.
CR-22.rationale: A federated session is bound to vault42's own lifetime. vault42 does not record the IdP's auth_time or force reauthentication when the maximum interval since the IdP authentication event elapses.
CR-22.compensating_control: The vault42 session is independently bounded by its own refresh TTL, is revocable by the user and by an administrator, and re-checks account state on every rotation.
CR-22.residual_risk: A user whose IdP session was terminated upstream keeps their vault42 session until it expires or is revoked.
CR-22.revisit_when: A deployment federates to an IdP whose session policy is the authoritative one, such as a corporate SSO with mandatory reauthentication.
CR-22.cost_of_closing: Record auth_time from the ID token and compare it on refresh.

CR-24.title: The audit log is not cryptographically chained and is not mirrored off-system
CR-24.security_md: Register-scoped. docs/security.md owns the AR-nn namespace and defines a different risk under this number; the two lists are deliberately disjoint.
CR-24.rationale: Hash chaining defends against an adversary who already holds database write access. Against that adversary a chain whose signing key lives in the same process is theatre: the adversary rewrites the rows and re-signs them. The honest version needs an off-box key and an off-system mirror, which is a deployment-topology commitment rather than a code change. Meanwhile the trigger and grant model already defeats the realistic adversary, a compromised vault_app role.
CR-24.compensating_control: audit.deny_modify() raises on UPDATE and DELETE; UPDATE and DELETE are revoked from vault_app; the one sanctioned deletion path is SECURITY DEFINER with a pinned search_path, EXECUTE revoked from PUBLIC, and the trigger re-enabled before it returns.
CR-24.residual_risk: An adversary holding database superuser access can rewrite history without leaving evidence in the log itself.
CR-24.revisit_when: 1.1, together with an off-system mirror. A chain designed without one would be worse than none because it would imply a guarantee it does not provide.
CR-24.cost_of_closing: A prev-hash column, a signing key held outside the process, read-time verification, and a checkpoint scheme that survives retention pruning. The batch insert path at internal/repository/postgres/audit.go:50 breaks a naive prev-hash chain and is the hard part.

CR-28.title: Email verification changes state on a GET
CR-28.security_md: Register-scoped. docs/security.md owns the AR-nn namespace and defines a different risk under this number; the two lists are deliberately disjoint.
CR-28.rationale: internal/server/server.go:490 mounts GET /auth/verify-email, and internal/handler/auth.go:298 mutates state on it by marking the address verified. ASVS V3.5.3 requires either a non-safe method or strict Sec-Fetch-* validation, and no Sec-Fetch-* header is read anywhere in the tree. The constraint is real rather than an oversight: the link is delivered by email and followed by a browser navigation, which is a GET, and turning it into a POST means an interstitial page the user must click through.
CR-28.compensating_control: The token is single-use and consumed atomically by a compare-and-delete, so a replayed or prefetched link verifies at most once; the token is high-entropy and short-lived; the effect is bounded to marking an address the operator already sent mail to as verified, and confers no session; the route is rate limited. This is the emailed-link pattern docs/security.md AR-1 already covers.
CR-28.residual_risk: A mail client, security scanner or link prefetcher that follows the link performs the verification without the user acting. Nothing else is reachable through the route.
CR-28.revisit_when: Any additional state change is added behind a GET route, or the verification link starts conferring a session rather than only marking an address verified.
CR-28.cost_of_closing: Either an interstitial page that POSTs the token, or Sec-Fetch-Site validation on the route. TestASVS_V3_5_3_StateChangingGETMatchesWhatTheRegisterClaims fails when either lands.

CR-29.title: The SPA and the API can be served from one origin
CR-29.security_md: Register-scoped. docs/security.md owns the AR-nn namespace and defines a different risk under this number; the two lists are deliberately disjoint.
CR-29.rationale: ASVS V3.5.4 wants separate applications on separate hostnames so the same-origin policy separates them. When VAULT_SERVE_FRONTEND is on, internal/server/server.go:875 mounts the embedded SPA at the catch-all route of the same server that answers /auth, /user and /client, so the two share an origin by construction and the policy separates nothing.
CR-29.compensating_control: VAULT_SERVE_FRONTEND is off by default (internal/config/config.go:527) and the chart ships it false (charts/vault/values.yaml), so the single-origin topology is opt-in; charts/vault/templates/frontend.yaml deploys the SPA as a separate nginx workload on its own hostname, which is the topology the requirement prefers and the one the chart documents; the session cookie is __Host- prefixed and SameSite=Strict, which does not depend on the origin split; the frontend CSP restricts script-src to 'self' with no unsafe-inline.
CR-29.residual_risk: An operator who enables the embedded frontend gives up the origin boundary between the SPA and the API, so an XSS in the SPA runs on the API's origin.
CR-29.revisit_when: The embedded frontend becomes the default, or the SPA gains a surface that renders content it did not author.
CR-29.cost_of_closing: Nothing to build. Closing it means documenting the separate-hostname topology as the supported production shape and keeping VAULT_SERVE_FRONTEND for development and the honeypot profile.

CR-30.title: Admin email HTML is validated by a regex denylist, not by a sanitisation library
CR-30.security_md: Register-scoped. docs/security.md owns the AR-nn namespace and defines a different risk under this number; the two lists are deliberately disjoint.
CR-30.rationale: ASVS V1.3.1 asks for a well-known and secure HTML sanitization library or framework feature. internal/email/templates.go:88 is a regex denylist. It blocks script, iframe, object, embed, base, link, svg and form tags, a meta only when that meta carries http-equiv, javascript: and data: URIs, css url(), on* event handlers, and the {{call and {{js template constructs. A denylist is the pattern the requirement exists to discourage, because it enumerates the badness it knows about. Filing this Not Applicable on "no WYSIWYG editor and no untrusted HTML input" skipped the fact that an HTML body does arrive in an HTTP request body and is stored and later compiled. An earlier version of this rationale also listed style among the blocked tags: it never was, and the pattern's own comment says a style block of inline CSS is allowed deliberately.
CR-30.compensating_control: The route requires rbac.EmailWrite, which is a super_admin-tier permission, so the population that can reach it is the population that could rewrite the mail wholesale anyway; the template is compiled with html/template, whose contextual auto-escaping means interpolated data cannot become markup; the output is an email body rendered by a mail client, not a page on vault42's origin, so there is no same-origin context to reach; every write is audited.
CR-30.residual_risk: A super_admin can put markup the denylist does not enumerate into an email body. The realistic outcome is a phishing-shaped mail, which the same principal could send by rewriting the copy.
CR-30.revisit_when: The template surface is opened to any role below super_admin, or an email template is ever rendered on vault42's own origin rather than delivered as mail.
CR-30.cost_of_closing: Replace the denylist with an allowlist sanitiser such as bluemonday, configured for an email-safe element set. The change is small; the reason it has not been made is that the denylist and the super_admin gate together already bound the realistic outcome.

CR-34.title: The Redis cache link has no TLS option
CR-34.security_md: Register-scoped. docs/security.md owns the AR-nn namespace and defines a different risk under this number; the two lists are deliberately disjoint.
CR-34.rationale: internal/redis/pool.go:184 dials TLS when Options.TLS is set, pinning tls.VersionTLS12 and verifying the server name. Nothing sets it. internal/cache/redis.go:19 builds the Options from address, password and database only; cache.NewCache passes no TLS argument, and no environment variable exists to supply one, so the branch is unreachable from any deployment. The cache link is therefore cleartext with no operator override, and it is the one connection in ASVS V12.3.1's own enumeration -- "middleware, databases" -- that vault42 does not encrypt now that the SMTP path fails closed. It carries the Redis AUTH password, sent on every new connection before any application traffic; rate-limit and lockout keys that embed client IP addresses and user identifiers; and the jti that binds a password-confirmation window. It does not carry the email one-time code, which is stored as an HMAC (internal/service/auth.go:1811).
CR-34.compensating_control: The chart deploys Redis as a workload beside vault and its NetworkPolicy admits port 6379 only from the vault pods, so the link is pod-to-pod inside one namespace rather than across a network the operator does not own; the same policy admits no egress to 443 at all. The AUTH secret is read from REDIS_PASS_FILE rather than the environment. Nothing durable transits the link: the cache holds short-TTL rate-limit counters, lockout markers, single-use challenge markers and an HMAC of the email one-time code, and every value that authorises anything is re-checked against the database or against a signed token before it is honoured.
CR-34.residual_risk: An attacker on the pod network between vault and Redis reads the AUTH password and the cache traffic, which includes client IP addresses and user identifiers. With the password they hold the cache: clearing a lockout marker or a rate-limit counter removes the throttle in front of password and one-time-code guessing. One escalation is sharper than the rest -- an attacker who already holds a stolen access token can write the confirmation record for that token's jti, which removes the password re-entry in front of DELETE /user/identity. No cache value is a credential on its own, and the database link is separately encrypted.
CR-34.revisit_when: Redis moves outside the pod network -- a managed cache, a shared cluster, a namespace under another team's policy -- or the cache starts holding a value that authorises something without a second check.
CR-34.cost_of_closing: A REDIS_TLS boolean and an optional server-name override on Config, threaded through cache.NewCache into the Options literal at internal/cache/redis.go:19. The dial path already exists at internal/redis/pool.go:184 and already pins tls.VersionTLS12, so internal/redis does not change. The chart then needs a Redis that terminates TLS, which is the part that is not a code change and is why this is scheduled rather than done.

requirements.requirement: Verify that input is decoded or unescaped into a canonical form only once, it is only decoded when encoded data in that form is expected, and that this is done before processing the input further, for example it is not performed after input validation or sanitization.
requirements.notes: Input is decoded once by net/http and encoding/json; sanitize.String escapes on the way out, not on the way in.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application performs output encoding and escaping either as a final step before being used by the interpreter for which it is intended or by the interpreter itself.
requirements.notes: Encoding is applied at the boundary of the interpreter that consumes the value.

requirements.requirement: Verify that output encoding for an HTTP response, HTML document, or XML document is relevant for the context required, such as encoding the relevant characters for HTML elements, HTML attributes, HTML comments, CSS, or HTTP header fields, to avoid changing the message or document structure.
requirements.notes: Responses are JSON produced by encoding/json, which escapes by construction; X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff stops a client reinterpreting them.

requirements.requirement: Verify that when dynamically building URLs, untrusted data is encoded according to its context (e.g., URL encoding or base64url encoding for query or path parameters). Ensure that only safe URL protocols are permitted (e.g., disallow javascript: or data:).
requirements.notes: RedirectPath rejects scheme-relative and absolute targets; AvatarURL is HTTPS-only.

requirements.requirement: Verify that output encoding or escaping is used when dynamically building JavaScript content (including JSON), to avoid changing the message or document structure (to avoid JavaScript and JSON injection).
requirements.notes: All JSON is produced by encoding/json. No response is assembled by string concatenation.

requirements.requirement: Verify that data selection or database queries (e.g., SQL, HQL, NoSQL, Cypher) use parameterized queries, ORMs, entity frameworks, or are otherwise protected from SQL Injection and other database injection attacks. This is also relevant when writing stored procedures.
requirements.notes: Every query in the repository layer is parameterised. Enforced structurally over all 139 call sites, with a negative control proving the detector fires.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application protects against OS command injection and that operating system calls use parameterized OS queries or use contextual command line output encoding.
requirements.notes: vault42 makes no operating-system calls. os/exec is not imported anywhere under internal/ or cmd/.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application protects against LDAP injection vulnerabilities, or that specific security controls to prevent LDAP injection have been implemented.
requirements.notes: No LDAP client. vault42 does not integrate with a directory service.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application is protected against XPath injection attacks by using query parameterization or precompiled queries.
requirements.notes: No XML or XPath processing anywhere in the tree.

requirements.requirement: Verify that LaTeX processors are configured securely (such as not using the "--shell-escape" flag) and an allowlist of commands is used to prevent LaTeX injection attacks.
requirements.notes: vault42 runs no LaTeX processor. Nothing in the tree renders documents; the only templating is Go html/template for the admin UI and email bodies.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application escapes special characters in regular expressions (typically using a backslash) to prevent them from being misinterpreted as metacharacters.
requirements.notes: Regular expressions are compiled from constants only; no request value is compiled as a pattern.

requirements.requirement: Verify that all untrusted HTML input from WYSIWYG editors or similar is sanitized using a well-known and secure HTML sanitization library or framework feature.
requirements.notes: Accepted risk CR-30. There is no WYSIWYG editor, but there is untrusted-shaped HTML input: an admin email template body arrives in an HTTP request and is stored. It is validated before storage (internal/adminapi/email.go:277) against a regex denylist (internal/email/templates.go:88) blocking script, iframe, object, embed, base, link, svg and form tags, javascript: and data: URIs, css url() and on* handlers. A denylist is the pattern this requirement exists to discourage, so the honest classification is an accepted risk with the three compensating controls named, not Not Applicable. The previous reason also cited internal/adminapi/email.go:346, which is inside PreviewEmailTemplate rather than the storage path.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application avoids the use of eval() or other dynamic code execution features such as Spring Expression Language (SpEL). Where there is no alternative, any user input being included must be sanitized before being executed.
requirements.notes: Go has no eval. No dynamic code execution feature is used.

requirements.requirement: Verify that data being passed to a potentially dangerous context is sanitized beforehand to enforce safety measures, such as only allowing characters which are safe for this context and trimming input which is too long.
requirements.notes: Values crossing into a dangerous context are constrained by the sanitize package.

requirements.requirement: Verify that user-supplied Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) scriptable content is validated or sanitized to contain only tags and attributes (such as draw graphics) that are safe for the application, e.g., do not contain scripts and foreignObject.
requirements.notes: No path accepts user-supplied SVG. The only surface on which SVG could arrive is an admin-authored email template, and the content validator rejects the svg tag along with the rest of the active-content families before the template is stored or previewed. TestASVS_V1_3_4_SVGAndActiveContentAreRejectedInEmailTemplates asserts the validator still names it.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application sanitizes or disables user-supplied scriptable or expression template language content, such as Markdown, CSS or XSL stylesheets, BBCode, or similar.
requirements.notes: The only operator-supplied styling input is the branding colour, constrained to a hex literal specifically to prevent CSS injection.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application protects against Server-side Request Forgery (SSRF) attacks, by validating untrusted data against an allowlist of protocols, domains, paths and ports and sanitizing potentially dangerous characters before using the data to call another service.
requirements.notes: The untrusted data this requirement names is the issuer's discovery document, and the four endpoints it supplies -- authorization_endpoint, token_endpoint, userinfo_endpoint and jwks_uri -- are the only outbound destinations vault42 takes from data rather than from configuration or a compiled-in literal. Protocol was already allowlisted by fetchableEndpoint (internal/oauth2/oidc.go:85). The domain, path and port half is now Policy.CheckDerived (internal/outbound/outbound.go:94), applied to all four before any of them is cached or used (internal/oauth2/oidc.go:184): an endpoint must name the issuer's own host, a subdomain of it on a label boundary, a loopback destination, or a host the operator listed in VAULT_OUTBOUND_ALLOWED_HOSTS. underDomain tests the suffix on a label boundary, so notokta.test is not admitted under okta.test. The rule needs no configuration and has no off switch: the nil Policy is the strict case. Policy.DialContext (internal/outbound/outbound.go:147) judges every address the destination resolved to and connects to the address it judged rather than re-resolving the name, which is what covers a name that resolves inward and a redirect that never passed through the endpoint check. cmd/vault/main.go:623 builds the deployment's Policy and installs it on every generic OIDC provider, asserted by TestVaultGuardsEveryOIDCProviderItBuilds. The refusal names the host and VAULT_OUTBOUND_ALLOWED_HOSTS, because the legitimate cross-domain provider is real. Previously accepted risk CR-17, now retired. No allowlist is applied to the six destinations that are compiled-in literals or operator-set URLs, deliberately: neither can be pointed anywhere by a request.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application protects against template injection attacks by not allowing templates to be built based on untrusted input. Where there is no alternative, any untrusted input being included dynamically during template creation must be sanitized or strictly validated.
requirements.notes: Met on the requirement's second clause, and by a stronger construction than before. A template really is built from input: an admin-supplied subject line and HTML body are parsed by html/template. What changed is where. The parse now lives in email.CompileOverride (internal/email/branding.go:63), which validates both strings (:70) before either reaches template.Parse (:80), and CompiledOverride can be constructed no other way -- so holding one is proof the content passed the checks. Validation used to run on the admin write path only, which meant a row reaching the table by any other route was compiled unvalidated on every send; it now runs wherever a stored override is loaded (internal/service/email_overrides.go:70). The admin write path still validates too (internal/adminapi/email.go:277), the routes still require rbac.EmailWrite, which is super_admin tier, and the package is still html/template, whose contextual auto-escaping leaves no OS or reflection escape hatch.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application appropriately sanitizes untrusted input before use in Java Naming and Directory Interface (JNDI) queries and that JNDI is configured securely to prevent JNDI injection attacks.
requirements.notes: JNDI is a Java mechanism and has no Go equivalent.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application sanitizes content before it is sent to memcache to prevent injection attacks.
requirements.notes: No memcache. The cache layer is Redis or in-process (internal/cache/).

requirements.requirement: Verify that format strings which might resolve in an unexpected or malicious way when used are sanitized before being processed.
requirements.notes: Format strings are constants throughout; go vet's printf analyser runs in CI and rejects a non-constant format.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application sanitizes user input before passing to mail systems to protect against SMTP or IMAP injection.
requirements.notes: sanitize.Email requires net/mail.ParseAddress to accept the address before it reaches the mail path, which rejects the embedded control characters SMTP injection needs.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application uses memory-safe string, safer memory copy and pointer arithmetic to detect or prevent stack, buffer, or heap overflows.
requirements.notes: Go is memory-safe. No unsafe package import exists under internal/ or cmd/.

requirements.requirement: Verify that sign, range, and input validation techniques are used to prevent integer overflows.
requirements.notes: Numeric request values are parsed with strconv and range-clamped before use. Handler.DeleteUser (internal/adminapi/handler.go:420) is the admin-plane entry point, writing the escrow record before the cascade.

requirements.requirement: Verify that dynamically allocated memory and resources are released, and that references or pointers to freed memory are removed or set to null to prevent dangling pointers and use-after-free vulnerabilities.
requirements.notes: Go is garbage-collected; there are no manual frees or dangling pointers. Resource handles (rows, bodies) are closed by defer.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application configures XML parsers to use a restrictive configuration and that unsafe features such as resolving external entities are disabled to prevent XML eXternal Entity (XXE) attacks.
requirements.notes: No XML parser is used.

requirements.requirement: Verify that deserialization of untrusted data enforces safe input handling, such as using an allowlist of object types or restricting client-defined object types, to prevent deserialization attacks. Deserialization mechanisms that are explicitly defined as insecure must not be used with untrusted input.
requirements.notes: Deserialisation is encoding/json into concrete structs with DisallowUnknownFields on the public API; there is no polymorphic or client-typed deserialisation anywhere.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application's documentation defines input validation rules for how to check the validity of data items against an expected structure. This could be common data formats such as credit card numbers, email addresses, telephone numbers, or it could be an internal data format.
requirements.notes: Per-field validation rules are specified in docs/spec.md and docs/api.md.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application's documentation defines how to validate the logical and contextual consistency of combined data items, such as checking that suburb and ZIP code match.
requirements.notes: IdentityData.Validate checks combined-field consistency (country against billing country, date of birth plausibility).

requirements.requirement: Verify that expectations for business logic limits and validations are documented, including both per-user and globally across the application.
requirements.notes: Per-user and global limits (session cap, rate limits, blob quotas, export cap) are documented in docs/config.md.

requirements.requirement: Verify that input is validated to enforce business or functional expectations for that input. This should either use positive validation against an allow list of values, patterns, and ranges, or be based on comparing the input to an expected structure and logical limits according to predefined rules. For L1, this can focus on input which is used to make specific business or security decisions. For L2 and up, this should apply to all input.
requirements.notes: Positive validation against expected shape, not denylisting.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application is designed to enforce input validation at a trusted service layer. While client-side validation improves usability and should be encouraged, it must not be relied upon as a security control.
requirements.notes: All validation is server-side; there is no client-side validation the server relies on.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application ensures that combinations of related data items are reasonable according to the pre-defined rules.
requirements.notes: Combined-item reasonableness is checked in the identity validator.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application will only process business logic flows for the same user in the expected sequential step order and without skipping steps.
requirements.notes: Multi-step flows are sequenced by single-use server-side state: the MFA challenge token gates CompleteMFALogin, and the OAuth verifier and exchange code are each consumed atomically.

requirements.requirement: Verify that business logic limits are implemented per the application's documentation to avoid business logic flaws being exploited.
requirements.notes: Met: CheckSessionLimit applies the documented concurrent-session-family cap, and the hard bound is CreateWithinCap on the insert, which takes an advisory lock so simultaneous logins cannot overshoot it. The OAuth callback used only the soft pre-check until this release; it now goes through CreateWithinCap too. The export cap and blob quotas implement the other documented limits.

requirements.requirement: Verify that transactions are being used at the business logic level such that either a business logic operation succeeds in its entirety or it is rolled back to the previous correct state.
requirements.notes: Multi-row operations that must be atomic (audit batch insert, erasure cascade) run in a transaction.

requirements.requirement: Verify that business logic level locking mechanisms are used to ensure that limited quantity resources (such as theater seats or delivery slots) cannot be double-booked by manipulating the application's logic.
requirements.notes: The concurrent-session cap is enforced as one unit of work on the paths that go through AuthService.storeRefreshToken: the new-family insert is issued through RefreshTokenRepository.CreateWithinCap, which counts the user's active families and inserts under a single per-user advisory lock, so simultaneous logins cannot each read the same free slot and overshoot the cap. A count-only pre-check still fails fast, and a login that loses the race is refused with the same too-many-sessions outcome. The path this row previously did not name is the social-login callback: internal/handler/oauth.go:641 calls CheckSessionLimit, a soft pre-check, and then inserts at :657 through the plain Create rather than CreateWithinCap, so two OAuth callbacks racing could each pass the pre-check and both insert. Two independent reviewers found the same gap; the evidence now names the path that was short rather than the two that were always fine. TestASVS_V2_3_4_EveryFamilyCreatingPathIsNamedByTheRegister enumerates every family-creating insert and requires this row to name any that does not use the capped insert, so the next one cannot be discovered by a reviewer instead of by CI.

requirements.requirement: Verify that anti-automation controls are in place to protect against excessive calls to application functions that could lead to data exfiltration, garbage-data creation, quota exhaustion, rate-limit breaches, denial-of-service, or overuse of costly resources.
requirements.notes: Per-user and per-IP rate limiting plus account lockout, fail-closed on the credential surface. The login limiter is 5 attempts in 15 minutes keyed by account with FailClosed set (internal/server/server.go:424); RateLimit (internal/middleware/ratelimit.go:266) is the middleware that enforces it, and every limiter is namespaced so two routes cannot share a bucket by accident.

requirements.requirement: Verify that security controls are in place to prevent browsers from rendering content or functionality in HTTP responses in an incorrect context (e.g., when an API, a user-uploaded file or other resource is requested directly). Possible controls could include: not serving the content unless HTTP request header fields (such as Sec-Fetch-\*) indicate it is the correct context, using the sandbox directive of the Content-Security-Policy header field or using the attachment disposition type in the Content-Disposition header field.
requirements.notes: All three of the controls this requirement names by example are now present. X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff is set on every response and default-src 'none' covers API paths; the third, the attachment disposition type, is set by attachmentDisposition (internal/handler/blob.go:434) on both download paths (internal/handler/blob.go:221 and :315), so a browser navigated straight at a blob URL saves the bytes instead of deciding for itself whether to render them. The test asserts the disposition type rather than the header's presence, because inline is also a Content-Disposition and is the rendering context this requirement exists to prevent. Previously accepted risk CR-26, now retired; Not Applicable before that.

requirements.requirement: Verify that content intended to be displayed as text, rather than rendered as HTML, is handled using safe rendering functions (such as createTextNode or textContent) to prevent unintended execution of content such as HTML or JavaScript.
requirements.notes: Safe text rendering is a property of the client-side rendering code in web/src, which the declared scope assesses separately. The Go server emits JSON; the one server-rendered markup surface, the admin email templates, is classified under V1.3.1 and V1.3.7 rather than here. The reason this row used to give was a claim about the shipped binary rather than about scope, and it was false.

requirements.requirement: Verify that cookies have the 'Secure' attribute set, and if the '\__Host-' prefix is not used for the cookie name, the '__Secure-' prefix must be used for the cookie name.
requirements.notes: Met: the __Host-refresh_token session cookie is issued with the Secure attribute (forced by the __Host- prefix and TLS) by the login handler. The live Set-Cookie is asserted by TestASVS_V3_3_1_LiveRefreshCookieIsSecure. Previously mis-marked Not Applicable on a "no browser-facing app" premise that the SPA route and session cookies contradict.

requirements.requirement: Verify that each cookie's 'SameSite' attribute value is set according to the purpose of the cookie, to limit exposure to user interface redress attacks and browser-based request forgery attacks, commonly known as cross-site request forgery (CSRF).
requirements.notes: Met: the refresh-token cookie sets SameSite=Strict on the live response, asserted by TestASVS_V3_3_2_LiveRefreshCookieSameSiteStrict. Previously mis-marked Not Applicable.

requirements.requirement: Verify that cookies have the '__Host-' prefix for the cookie name unless they are explicitly designed to be shared with other hosts.
requirements.notes: Met: the session cookie uses the __Host- prefix (__Host-refresh_token), asserted on the live response by TestASVS_V3_3_3_LiveRefreshCookieHostPrefix. Previously mis-marked Not Applicable.

requirements.requirement: Verify that if the value of a cookie is not meant to be accessible to client-side scripts (such as a session token), the cookie must have the 'HttpOnly' attribute set and the same value (e. g. session token) must only be transferred to the client via the 'Set-Cookie' header field.
requirements.notes: Met: the refresh-token cookie sets HttpOnly on the live response, asserted by TestASVS_V3_3_4_LiveRefreshCookieHttpOnly. Previously mis-marked Not Applicable.

requirements.requirement: Verify that a Strict-Transport-Security header field is included on all responses to enforce an HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) policy. A maximum age of at least 1 year must be defined, and for L2 and up, the policy must apply to all subdomains as well.
requirements.notes: Met: Strict-Transport-Security (max-age >= 1 year, includeSubDomains, preload) is set on every response by the security-headers middleware, asserted by TestOWASP_A02_2025_SecurityHeadersAreSetOnEveryResponse. Previously mis-marked Not Applicable.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) Access-Control-Allow-Origin header field is a fixed value by the application, or if the Origin HTTP request header field value is used, it is validated against an allowlist of trusted origins. When 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *' needs to be used, verify that the response does not include any sensitive information.
requirements.notes: Met: the CORS middleware builds an allowlist set from the configured origin plus any additional origins (internal/middleware/cors.go:27) and reflects the request Origin only on a hit (:51). An origin that is not on the list gets no Access-Control-Allow-Origin at all, and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is withheld from the wildcard (:64), so the requirement's second clause holds too. Dev allow-all reflects localhost origins only. TestASVS_V3_4_2_CORSReflectsOnlyAllowlistedOrigins drives the middleware with four unlisted origins including a suffix-confusion host and a scheme downgrade. Previously Not Applicable on the false premise that vault42 serves no browser-facing application.

requirements.requirement: Verify that HTTP responses include a Content-Security-Policy response header field which defines directives to ensure the browser only loads and executes trusted content or resources, in order to limit execution of malicious JavaScript. As a minimum, a global policy must be used which includes the directives object-src 'none' and base-uri 'none' and defines either an allowlist or uses nonces or hashes. For an L3 application, a per-response policy with nonces or hashes must be defined.
requirements.notes: Met: both Content-Security-Policy strings now declare the two directives this requirement names as the minimum. apiCSP is default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none' (internal/middleware/security_headers.go:18) and frontendCSP adds them to its allowlisted default-src 'self' policy (:19). Both matter because the two are chosen per request path, so a directive on one is a directive on some of the responses. base-uri has no fallback at all -- it is not a fetch directive -- so an injected <base> would re-point every relative URL while default-src 'self' reported itself satisfied. Carried as accepted risk CR-27 until the directives landed; TestASVS_V3_4_3_TheCSPMatchesWhatTheRegisterClaims fired on the merge and required this row to move.

requirements.requirement: Verify that all HTTP responses contain an 'X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff' header field. This instructs browsers not to use content sniffing and MIME type guessing for the given response, and to require the response's Content-Type header field value to match the destination resource. For example, the response to a request for a style is only accepted if the response's Content-Type is 'text/css'. This also enables the use of the Cross-Origin Read Blocking (CORB) functionality by the browser.
requirements.notes: Met: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff is set on every response, asserted by TestOWASP_A02_2025_SecurityHeadersAreSetOnEveryResponse. Previously mis-marked Not Applicable.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application sets a referrer policy to prevent leakage of technically sensitive data to third-party services via the 'Referer' HTTP request header field. This can be done using the Referrer-Policy HTTP response header field or via HTML element attributes. Sensitive data could include path and query data in the URL, and for internal non-public applications also the hostname.
requirements.notes: Met: Referrer-Policy: no-referrer is set on every response, asserted by TestOWASP_A02_2025_SecurityHeadersAreSetOnEveryResponse. Previously mis-marked Not Applicable.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the web application uses the frame-ancestors directive of the Content-Security-Policy header field for every HTTP response to ensure that it cannot be embedded by default and that embedding of specific resources is allowed only when necessary. Note that the X-Frame-Options header field, although supported by browsers, is obsolete and may not be relied upon.
requirements.notes: Met: anti-framing is enforced on every response via CSP frame-ancestors none and X-Frame-Options: DENY, asserted by TestOWASP_A02_2025_SecurityHeadersAreSetOnEveryResponse. Previously mis-marked Not Applicable.

requirements.requirement: Verify that, if the application does not rely on the CORS preflight mechanism to prevent disallowed cross-origin requests to use sensitive functionality, these requests are validated to ensure they originate from the application itself. This may be done by using and validating anti-forgery tokens or requiring extra HTTP header fields that are not CORS-safelisted request-header fields. This is to defend against browser-based request forgery attacks, commonly known as cross-site request forgery (CSRF).
requirements.notes: Met: POST /auth/refresh authenticates from a cookie rather than a bearer token (internal/handler/auth.go:121 reads r.Cookie(refreshTokenCookie)), which is exactly the shape this requirement addresses. The anti-forgery control is the cookie itself: SameSite=Strict (internal/handler/auth.go:316) means the browser does not attach it to a cross-site request, so a forged request arrives unauthenticated. __Host- prefix, HttpOnly and Secure close the fixation and script-read variants. TestASVS_V3_5_1_TheCookieAuthenticatedRouteIsProtectedBySameSiteStrict drives a real login and reads the live Set-Cookie. Previously Not Applicable, which discarded a working control.

requirements.requirement: Verify that, if the application relies on the CORS preflight mechanism to prevent disallowed cross-origin use of sensitive functionality, it is not possible to call the functionality with a request which does not trigger a CORS-preflight request. This may require checking the values of the 'Origin' and 'Content-Type' request header fields or using an extra header field that is not a CORS-safelisted header-field.
requirements.notes: Met: the preflight response names a closed header set, Content-Type, Authorization and DPoP (internal/middleware/cors.go:62), with no wildcard, and OPTIONS is answered 204 by the middleware (:68). Every authenticated route requires Authorization, which is not a CORS-safelisted request header, so a cross-origin call to sensitive functionality always preflights; a simple request that skips preflight arrives without it and is answered 401. TestASVS_V3_5_2_SensitiveFunctionalityAlwaysTriggersPreflight asserts both halves. Previously Not Applicable.

requirements.requirement: Verify that HTTP requests to sensitive functionality use appropriate HTTP methods such as POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE, and not methods defined by the HTTP specification as "safe" such as HEAD, OPTIONS, or GET. Alternatively, strict validation of the Sec-Fetch-* request header fields can be used to ensure that the request did not originate from an inappropriate cross-origin call, a navigation request, or a resource load (such as an image source) where this is not expected.
requirements.notes: Accepted risk CR-28. GET /auth/verify-email mutates state: it marks an address verified. The requirement offers two ways out, a non-safe method or strict Sec-Fetch-* validation, and vault42 has neither. What bounds it is a single-use token consumed atomically, and the emailed-link pattern is the one docs/security.md AR-1 already covers. TestASVS_V3_5_3_StateChangingGETMatchesWhatTheRegisterClaims fails when either remedy lands. Previously Not Applicable, which is how this stayed invisible.

requirements.requirement: Verify that separate applications are hosted on different hostnames to leverage the restrictions provided by same-origin policy, including how documents or scripts loaded by one origin can interact with resources from another origin and hostname-based restrictions on cookies.
requirements.notes: Accepted risk CR-29. When VAULT_SERVE_FRONTEND is on, the SPA and the API answer on one origin by construction (internal/server/server.go:667 mounts the SPA at the catch-all route), so the same-origin policy separates neither from the other. That is a deployment choice with a residual, not an inapplicable requirement: the chart also ships a separate frontend deployment, which is the topology the requirement prefers, and the default is VAULT_SERVE_FRONTEND=false. Previously Not Applicable.

requirements.requirement: Verify that messages received by the postMessage interface are discarded if the origin of the message is not trusted, or if the syntax of the message is invalid.
requirements.notes: postMessage is a browser API. Its use, and any origin check on it, live in web/src, which the declared scope assesses separately. The reason this row used to give was a claim about the shipped binary rather than about scope, and it was false.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application only uses client-side technologies which are still supported and considered secure. Examples of technologies which do not meet this requirement include NSAPI plugins, Flash, Shockwave, ActiveX, Silverlight, NACL, or client-side Java applets.
requirements.notes: Met: the shipped client is Vue 3 built by Vite, both currently supported. TestASVS_V3_7_1_NoObsoletePluginTechnologyIsShipped scans the embedded SPA entry point and the source index for the markup by which every technology the requirement names is loaded: applet, embed, Shockwave and Silverlight MIME types, an ActiveX classid, Native Client, .swf and .xap. Previously Not Applicable.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application will only automatically redirect the user to a different hostname or domain (which is not controlled by the application) where the destination appears on an allowlist.
requirements.notes: Met: every http.Redirect in the shipped tree is in internal/handler/oauth.go, and every target is either the operator-configured origin plus a literal path, or the upstream provider authorize URL built from a static provider map and gated on isSafeAuthorizeRedirect (internal/handler/oauth.go:126, defined at :172), which requires an absolute https URL. No redirect_uri, next or return_to parameter is read anywhere. TestASVS_V3_7_2_EveryRedirectTargetIsServerControlled resolves each target through its assignments and fails on a new redirect whose target is request-derived. Previously Not Applicable.

requirements.requirement: Verify that every HTTP response with a message body contains a Content-Type header field that matches the actual content of the response, including the charset parameter to specify safe character encoding (e.g., UTF-8, ISO-8859-1) according to IANA Media Types, such as "text/", "/+xml" and "/xml".
requirements.notes: WriteJSON sets application/json on every body-bearing response.

requirements.requirement: Verify that only user-facing endpoints (intended for manual web-browser access) automatically redirect from HTTP to HTTPS, while other services or endpoints do not implement transparent redirects. This is to avoid a situation where a client is erroneously sending unencrypted HTTP requests, but since the requests are being automatically redirected to HTTPS, the leakage of sensitive data goes undiscovered.
requirements.notes: The API does not redirect; HSTS instructs browsers to use HTTPS for the browser-facing origin.

requirements.requirement: Verify that any HTTP header field used by the application and set by an intermediary layer, such as a load balancer, a web proxy, or a backend-for-frontend service, cannot be overridden by the end-user. Example headers might include X-Real-IP, X-Forwarded-*, or X-User-ID.
requirements.notes: X-Forwarded-For is honoured only when a trusted-proxy list is configured, and the walk takes the rightmost untrusted hop.

requirements.requirement: Verify that all application components (including load balancers, firewalls, and application servers) determine boundaries of incoming HTTP messages using the appropriate mechanism for the HTTP version to prevent HTTP request smuggling. In HTTP/1.x, if a Transfer-Encoding header field is present, the Content-Length header must be ignored per RFC 2616. When using HTTP/2 or HTTP/3, if a Content-Length header field is present, the receiver must ensure that it is consistent with the length of the DATA frames.
requirements.notes: net/http rejects conflicting Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding framing; MaxHeaderBytes bounds the header block.

requirements.requirement: Verify that a query allowlist, depth limiting, amount limiting, or query cost analysis is used to prevent GraphQL or data layer expression Denial of Service (DoS) as a result of expensive, nested queries.
requirements.notes: vault42 exposes no GraphQL endpoint and no other query language over HTTP. The API is a fixed set of REST routes enumerated in internal/server/server.go.

requirements.requirement: Verify that GraphQL introspection queries are disabled in the production environment unless the GraphQL API is meant to be used by other parties.
requirements.notes: vault42 exposes no GraphQL endpoint, so there is no introspection query to disable.

requirements.requirement: Verify that WebSocket over TLS (WSS) is used for all WebSocket connections.
requirements.notes: vault42 opens no WebSocket connections. Every route is a request-response HTTP handler; no upgrade handler exists in the route table.

requirements.requirement: Verify that, during the initial HTTP WebSocket handshake, the Origin header field is checked against a list of origins allowed for the application.
requirements.notes: vault42 performs no WebSocket handshake, so there is no upgrade request whose Origin header could be checked.

requirements.requirement: Verify that, if the application's standard session management cannot be used, dedicated tokens are being used for this, which comply with the relevant Session Management security requirements.
requirements.notes: vault42 has no WebSocket channel, so no dedicated out-of-band session token is needed alongside the standard mechanism.

requirements.requirement: Verify that dedicated WebSocket session management tokens are initially obtained or validated through the previously authenticated HTTPS session when transitioning an existing HTTPS session to a WebSocket channel.
requirements.notes: vault42 has no WebSocket channel, so there is no separate token to obtain through an authenticated HTTPS session.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the documentation defines the permitted file types, expected file extensions, and maximum size (including unpacked size) for each upload feature. Additionally, ensure that the documentation specifies how files are made safe for end-users to download and process, such as how the application behaves when a malicious file is detected.
requirements.notes: Both clauses are documented. The size clause was already met: docs/api.md carries the label cap, the minimum and maximum blob size, the per-user byte quota and the rejection behaviour, and now states explicitly that there are no permitted file types or extensions to define, because the stored object is an opaque octet stream the server never parses and the named-blob charset excludes the dot, so the unpacked size equals the stored size. The clause that was open -- how stored objects are made safe for an end user to download -- is the 'How stored objects are made safe to download' section, which records that every read is scoped to the caller's own pseudonym, that attachmentDisposition (internal/handler/blob.go:434) marks both download paths as attachments, that the filename is the server's own reference rather than anything a caller supplied, and that nosniff and a default-src 'none' CSP bound what a browser will do with the response. The test reads the header off the shipped handler as well as the prose, so the document cannot describe a control the code does not set. Previously accepted risk CR-26, now retired; Not Applicable before that on the false premise that vault42 accepts no uploads.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application will only accept files of a size which it can process without causing a loss of performance or a denial of service attack.
requirements.notes: Met: every write path wraps the body in http.MaxBytesReader sized from the configured maximum plus 1 KiB of slack, so an oversized body is refused at the reader rather than buffered and then measured. POST /user/blobs at internal/handler/blob.go:38, PUT /user/blobs/named/{name} at :143, and PUT /service/documents/{subject}/{key} at internal/handler/servicedoc.go:142, which re-applies its own limit because that route prefix is exempt from the global 8 KiB cap. TestASVS_V5_2_1_OversizedUploadsAreRefusedAtTheReader posts four times the maximum on two paths and asserts nothing reaches the repository. Previously Not Applicable.

requirements.requirement: Verify that when the application accepts a file, either on its own or within an archive such as a zip file, it checks if the file extension matches an expected file extension and validates that the contents correspond to the type represented by the extension. This includes, but is not limited to, checking the initial 'magic bytes', performing image re-writing, and using specialized libraries for file content validation. For L1, this can focus just on files which are used to make specific business or security decisions. For L2 and up, this must apply to all files being accepted.
requirements.notes: There is no extension or declared type to validate against. The stored object arrives as an octet stream or as a multipart part whose bytes the server compresses and encrypts without interpreting, and the one caller-supplied identifier, the named-blob reference, is restricted to a charset that excludes the dot, so a reference cannot carry an extension in the first place. TestASVS_V5_3_2_CallerSuppliedBlobNamesAreStrictlyValidated asserts the charset. The previous reason claimed vault42 accepts no uploads, which the multipart branch at internal/handler/blob.go:52 contradicts.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application checks compressed files (e.g., zip, gz, docx, odt) against maximum allowed uncompressed size and against maximum number of files before uncompressing the file.
requirements.notes: Met: blobs are deflate-compressed on write and inflated on read, and the read path is bounded by const maxDecompressedSize = 10 MiB (internal/service/blob.go:255) with an io.LimitReader at maxDecompressedSize+1 (:257). The extra byte is what makes over-limit distinguishable from exactly-at-limit, so a bomb is rejected with an explicit error (:260) rather than silently truncated and returned as intact. TestASVS_V5_2_3_DecompressionIsBoundedAndFailsClosed asserts the round trip and all three properties. Previously Not Applicable, which reported a working decompression-bomb defence as a feature that did not exist.

requirements.requirement: Verify that files uploaded or generated by untrusted input and stored in a public folder, are not executed as server-side program code when accessed directly with an HTTP request.
requirements.notes: Stored objects are database rows, not files in a folder, so there is no path at which one could be requested directly and no server-side interpreter that would execute it. TestASVS_V5_3_1_And_V5_4_3_StoredBytesTouchNoFilesystemAndReachNoOtherUser asserts the blob handler and service reach the filesystem through no writer at all. The previous reason claimed vault42 accepts no uploads.

requirements.requirement: Verify that when the application creates file paths for file operations, instead of user-submitted filenames, it uses internally generated or trusted data, or if user-submitted filenames or file metadata must be used, strict validation and sanitization must be applied. This is to protect against path traversal, local or remote file inclusion (LFI, RFI), and server-side request forgery (SSRF) attacks.
requirements.notes: Met: PUT /user/blobs/named/{name} stores under a caller-supplied name, so the requirement's second branch applies and strict validation is what it asks for. validRefName (internal/handler/blob.go:376, called at :138) restricts the name to [a-zA-Z0-9_-], which excludes every path separator, dot, NUL and shell metacharacter; the length is capped at 255 runes (:134). The stored object is a database row keyed by an HMAC of the name, never a filesystem path. TestASVS_V5_3_2_CallerSuppliedBlobNamesAreStrictlyValidated drives eleven traversal and injection shapes plus a positive control. Previously Not Applicable on the claim that no name is ever caller-supplied.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application validates or ignores user-submitted filenames, including in a JSON, JSONP, or URL parameter and specifies a filename in the Content-Disposition header field in the response.
requirements.notes: Both clauses hold. Caller-submitted names are validated by validRefName before use (internal/handler/blob.go:376), and both download paths now specify a filename through attachmentDisposition (internal/handler/blob.go:434). The filename is the blob's own reference reduced by contentDispositionFilename (internal/handler/blob.go:409) to [A-Za-z0-9._-] and capped at maxDispositionFilename, with everything else dropped rather than escaped, falling back to a fixed literal when nothing usable remains. Dropping rather than escaping is deliberate: DownloadNamed reads its name straight out of the route and never runs validRefName, so the response header cannot borrow the upload path's guarantee, and a quote that survived would open a second parameter. Previously accepted risk CR-26, now retired; Not Applicable before that.

requirements.requirement: Verify that file names served (e.g., in HTTP response header fields or email attachments) are encoded or sanitized (e.g., following RFC 6266) to preserve document structure and prevent injection attacks.
requirements.notes: Met by the sanitisation branch the requirement offers. A caller-chosen label carrying CR, LF or NUL is rejected at the boundary with invalid_label (internal/handler/blob.go:85), and the serve path sanitises again through sanitizeLabelForHeader (:384, applied at :220 and :315), which drops U+0000-U+001F before the value becomes the X-Blob-Label response header. That is what closes response-header injection. Limitation recorded rather than hidden: non-ASCII is passed through un-encoded rather than RFC 8187 encoded, which is a fidelity limit in a custom header, not an injection channel. TestASVS_V5_4_2_ServedLabelsCannotForgeResponseHeaders drives a real multipart upload with a response-splitting payload and a benign positive control. Previously Not Applicable.

requirements.requirement: Verify that files obtained from untrusted sources are scanned by antivirus scanners to prevent serving of known malicious content.
requirements.notes: There is no antivirus integration, and what makes that defensible is that the scanner's purpose, stopping known-malicious content being served on to somebody else, has no reachable path here: every read is scoped to the pseudonym derived from the caller's own authenticated subject, so a stored object is only ever returned to the account that stored it. TestASVS_V5_3_1_And_V5_4_3_StoredBytesTouchNoFilesystemAndReachNoOtherUser asserts every read is keyed by claims.Subject. The previous reason claimed vault42 accepts no uploads.

requirements.requirement: Verify that application documentation defines how controls such as rate limiting, anti-automation, and adaptive response, are used to defend against attacks such as credential stuffing and password brute force. The documentation must make clear how these controls are configured and prevent malicious account lockout.
requirements.notes: Rate limiting, lockout and breach-corpus checking are specified in docs/spec.md and wired at the route table: loginRL, registerRL and passwordResetRL are constructed with FailClosed and a VPN-scrutiny weight (internal/server/server.go:424).

requirements.requirement: Verify that a list of context-specific words is documented in order to prevent their use in passwords. The list could include permutations of organization names, product names, system identifiers, project codenames, department or role names, and similar.
requirements.notes: The blocked set is the HIBP breach corpus rather than a hand-maintained word list, which subsumes the context-specific list.

requirements.requirement: Verify that, if the application includes multiple authentication pathways, these are all documented together with the security controls and authentication strength which must be consistently enforced across them.
requirements.notes: The three authentication pathways (password, federated, client credentials) are documented with their strength.

requirements.requirement: Verify that user set passwords are at least 8 characters in length although a minimum of 15 characters is strongly recommended.
requirements.notes: Met. This requirement asks for 8 and strongly recommends 15; vault42 enforces 15. passwordMinLengthFloor (internal/config/config.go:975) is 15 and a non-dev profile refuses to start below it (:622); the dev profile carries a lower floor of 8, which is still this requirement's own minimum. The evidence previously cited internal/config/config.go:432, a doc comment on the RecoveryRetentionPeriod field, which has nothing to do with password length.

requirements.requirement: Verify that users can change their password.
requirements.notes: POST /user/password. Test repointed in the register-integrity pass to a case that exercises the clause directly.

requirements.requirement: Verify that password change functionality requires the user's current and new password.
requirements.notes: The change endpoint is behind confirmMw, which requires the current password.

requirements.requirement: Verify that passwords submitted during account registration or password change are checked against an available set of, at least, the top 3000 passwords which match the application's password policy, e.g. minimum length.
requirements.notes: Checked against the full HIBP corpus by k-anonymity range query, which is a superset of the top 3000.

requirements.requirement: Verify that passwords of any composition can be used, without rules limiting the type of characters permitted. There must be no requirement for a minimum number of upper or lower case characters, numbers, or special characters.
requirements.notes: No composition rules of any kind.

requirements.requirement: Verify that password input fields use type=password to mask the entry. Applications may allow the user to temporarily view the entire masked password, or the last typed character of the password.
requirements.notes: Masking a password field is a property of the rendering client. The API surface is JSON over HTTP; the only input the server sees is a decoded request body, and how the field that produced it was rendered is decided in web/src, which the declared scope assesses separately.

requirements.requirement: Verify that "paste" functionality, browser password helpers, and external password managers are permitted.
requirements.notes: The API imposes no paste or manager restriction; the password is accepted as submitted.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application verifies the user's password exactly as received from the user, without any modifications such as truncation or case transformation.
requirements.notes: No truncation and no case transformation; Unicode is preserved.

requirements.requirement: Verify that passwords of at least 64 characters are permitted.
requirements.notes: Maximum length permits at least 64 characters.

requirements.requirement: Verify that a user's password stays valid until it is discovered to be compromised or the user rotates it. The application must not require periodic credential rotation.
requirements.notes: No periodic rotation is imposed.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the documented list of context specific words is used to prevent easy to guess passwords being created.
requirements.notes: The breach corpus is the enforced list.

requirements.requirement: Verify that passwords submitted during account registration or password changes are checked against a set of breached passwords.
requirements.notes: Checked on registration and change.

requirements.requirement: Verify that controls to prevent attacks such as credential stuffing and password brute force are implemented according to the application's security documentation.
requirements.notes: Per-user lockout at 5 in 15 minutes, per-IP at 20, fail-closed limiters on the credential surface (internal/server/server.go:424 constructs loginRL at Limit 5 over a 15-minute window).

requirements.requirement: Verify that default user accounts (e.g., "root", "admin", or "sa") are not present in the application or are disabled.
requirements.notes: No default account exists. EnsureFirstAdmin (internal/adminapi/auth.go:412) creates the first-boot super admin with a 32-byte CSPRNG password (:452), delivered through firstboot.Deliver rather than the process log, and the dev seed file is loaded only when VAULT_SEED_FILE names it explicitly.

requirements.requirement: Verify that either a multi-factor authentication mechanism or a combination of single-factor authentication mechanisms, must be used in order to access the application. For L3, one of the factors must be a hardware-based authentication mechanism which provides compromise and impersonation resistance against phishing attacks while verifying the intent to authenticate by requiring a user-initiated action (such as a button press on a FIDO hardware key or a mobile phone). Relaxing any of the considerations in this requirement requires a fully documented rationale and a comprehensive set of mitigating controls.
requirements.notes: TOTP, WebAuthn, email OTP and backup codes are all available as second factors, and MFA can be required globally.

requirements.requirement: Verify that, if the application includes multiple authentication pathways, there are no undocumented pathways and that security controls and authentication strength are enforced consistently.
requirements.notes: Every route is enumerated by the structural route scan against a declared public allowlist, so an undocumented pathway fails the build. The unauthenticated entries are deliberate and few -- GET /auth/verify-email at internal/server/server.go:504 is one, reached from an emailed link and carrying its own rate limiter.

requirements.requirement: Verify that users are notified of suspicious authentication attempts (successful or unsuccessful). This may include authentication attempts from an unusual location or client, partially successful authentication (only one of multiple factors), an authentication attempt after a long period of inactivity or a successful authentication after several unsuccessful attempts.
requirements.notes: Met: a login from a new country for the account triggers an out-of-band, throttled notification (internal/service/auth.go notifyNewCountry), with country derived locally from the embedded IP-intelligence table (internal/ipintel), country granularity only and the IP never stored, logged or emailed. VPN/hosting/Tor origins are additionally given heavier rate-limit scrutiny without being blocked. Asserted by TestASVS_AR18_NewLocationNoticeAndVPNScrutiny.

requirements.requirement: Verify that email is not used as either a single-factor or multi-factor authentication mechanism.
requirements.notes: Email OTP exists but is not sufficient alone; a password is always required first. L3 requirement, recorded for completeness.

requirements.requirement: Verify that users are notified after updates to authentication details, such as credential resets or modification of the username or email address.
requirements.notes: Credential changes notify and revoke all sessions.

requirements.requirement: Verify that valid users cannot be deduced from failed authentication challenges, such as by basing on error messages, HTTP response codes, or different response times. Registration and forgot password functionality must also have this protection.
requirements.notes: All four login outcomes that once differed by status code without a valid password now answer 401 invalid_credentials. account_locked and the import-claim path burn the same dummy Argon2 and mask; banned and disabled are revealed only after a successful password verification, so a caller without the password cannot tell any account state from an unknown address, and timing is equalised by the dummy-hash path. This L3 requirement is met above the assessed L2 baseline.

requirements.requirement: Verify that system generated initial passwords or activation codes are securely randomly generated, follow the existing password policy, and expire after a short period of time or after they are initially used. These initial secrets must not be permitted to become the long term password.
requirements.notes: System-generated credentials are CSPRNG-derived, single-use and short-lived; the first-boot admin password is 32 bytes from vaultcrypto.RandomBytes (internal/adminapi/auth.go:452).

requirements.requirement: Verify that password hints or knowledge-based authentication (so-called "secret questions") are not present.
requirements.notes: No password hints and no knowledge-based authentication. Test repointed in the register-integrity pass to a case that exercises the clause directly.

requirements.requirement: Verify that a secure process for resetting a forgotten password is implemented, that does not bypass any enabled multi-factor authentication mechanisms.
requirements.notes: Reset consumes a single-use token and revokes every session; it does not bypass MFA.

requirements.requirement: Verify that if a multi-factor authentication factor is lost, evidence of identity proofing is performed at the same level as during enrollment.
requirements.notes: Factor loss is handled by the operator-held recovery escrow rather than by re-running identity proofing, because vault42 performs no identity proofing at enrollment and therefore has no level to match. The escrow requires an offline private key held outside the system.

requirements.requirement: Verify that lookup secrets, out-of-band authentication requests or codes, and time-based one-time passwords (TOTPs) are only successfully usable once.
requirements.notes: TOTP codes and backup codes are single-use.

requirements.requirement: Verify that, when being stored in the application's backend, lookup secrets with less than 112 bits of entropy (19 random alphanumeric characters or 34 random digits) are hashed with an approved password storage hashing algorithm that incorporates a 32-bit random salt. A standard hash function can be used if the secret has 112 bits of entropy or more.
requirements.notes: Backup codes are hashed before storage.

requirements.requirement: Verify that lookup secrets, out-of-band authentication code, and time-based one-time password seeds, are generated using a Cryptographically Secure Pseudorandom Number Generator (CSPRNG) to avoid predictable values.
requirements.notes: All secrets come from crypto/rand.

requirements.requirement: Verify that lookup secrets and out-of-band authentication codes have a minimum of 20 bits of entropy (typically 4 random alphanumeric characters or 6 random digits is sufficient).
requirements.notes: Backup codes carry well above 20 bits of entropy.

requirements.requirement: Verify that out-of-band authentication requests, codes, or tokens, as well as time-based one-time passwords (TOTPs) have a defined lifetime. Out of band requests must have a maximum lifetime of 10 minutes and for TOTP a maximum lifetime of 30 seconds.
requirements.notes: TOTP period is 30 seconds with a bounded skew window; email OTP has an explicit expiry.

requirements.requirement: Verify that any authentication factor (including physical devices) can be revoked in case of theft or other loss.
requirements.notes: Every factor can be removed by its owner after re-confirmation. L3 requirement, recorded for completeness.

requirements.requirement: Verify that biometric authentication mechanisms are only used as secondary factors together with either something you have or something you know.
requirements.notes: vault42 implements no biometric verifier of its own. Platform biometrics reach it only through WebAuthn, where the authenticator performs the comparison and vault42 sees a cryptographic assertion.

requirements.requirement: Verify that time-based one-time passwords (TOTPs) are checked based on a time source from a trusted service and not from an untrusted or client provided time.
requirements.notes: TOTP is computed from the server clock; no client-supplied time is accepted. L3 requirement, recorded for completeness.

requirements.requirement: Verify that authentication mechanisms using the Public Switched Telephone Network (PSTN) to deliver One-time Passwords (OTPs) via phone or SMS are offered only when the phone number has previously been validated, alternate stronger methods (such as Time based One-time Passwords) are also offered, and the service provides information on their security risks to users. For L3 applications, phone and SMS must not be available as options.
requirements.notes: vault42 sends no OTP over the PSTN. There is no SMS or voice channel.

requirements.requirement: Verify that out-of-band authentication requests, codes, or tokens are bound to the original authentication request for which they were generated and are not usable for a previous or subsequent one.
requirements.notes: The MFA challenge token binds the second factor to the login attempt that produced it. Test repointed in the register-integrity pass to a case that exercises the clause directly.

requirements.requirement: Verify that a code based out-of-band authentication mechanism is protected against brute force attacks by using rate limiting. Consider also using a code with at least 64 bits of entropy.
requirements.notes: The email-OTP and TOTP endpoints carry fail-closed rate limiters: totpRL is 5 in 5 minutes keyed by IP with FailClosed set (internal/server/server.go:436) and is mounted on the TOTP verify route (:546).

requirements.requirement: Verify that, where push notifications are used for multi-factor authentication, rate limiting is used to prevent push bombing attacks. Number matching may also mitigate this risk.
requirements.notes: vault42 offers no push-notification authentication factor. The out-of-band factor is an emailed code, which is pull-based and rate-limited, so push bombing has no channel.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the certificates used to verify cryptographic authentication assertions are stored in a way protects them from modification.
requirements.notes: This requirement is about protecting the trust store used to verify certificate-based authentication assertions. vault42 derives user identity from passwords, TOTP, WebAuthn and federated OIDC, and from none of them a peer certificate. Real client-certificate verification does exist, at cmd/admin-gateway/main.go:263, where the admin gateway sets ClientAuth: RequireAndVerifyClientCert against a ClientCAs pool loaded from cfg.ClientCAFile at :249 -- but that is a transport gate, not a user assertion: nothing extracts an identity from the peer certificate, and admin identity still comes from the session afterwards, which is what docs/security.md AR-9 records. The trust store itself is assessed under V12.1.3. The previous reason implied that certificate verification happens nowhere, which reads as a stronger statement than the code supports.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the challenge nonce is at least 64 bits in length, and statistically unique or unique over the lifetime of the cryptographic device.
requirements.notes: WebAuthn challenges are 32 CSPRNG bytes. L3 requirement, recorded for completeness.
